See the GNU General Public License * version 2 for more details (a copy is included in the LICENSE file that * accompanied this code). * * You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License version * 2 along with this work; if not, write to the Free Software Foundation, * Inc., 51 Franklin St, Fifth Floor, Boston, MA 02110-1301 USA. * * Please contact Oracle, 500 Oracle Parkway, Redwood Shores, CA 94065 USA * or visit www.oracle.com if you need additional information or have any * questions. */ /* * This file is available under and governed by the GNU General Public * License version 2 only, as published by the Free Software Foundation. * However, the following notice accompanied the original version of this * file: * * Written by Doug Lea with assistance from members of JCP JSR-166 * Expert Group and released to the public domain, as explained at * http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/ */ package java.util.concurrent; /** * A task that returns a result and may throw an exception. * Implementors define a single method with no arguments called * {@code call}. * *

The {@code Callable} interface is similar to {@link * java.lang.Runnable}, in that both are designed for classes whose * instances are potentially executed by another thread. A * {@code Runnable}, however, does not return a result and cannot * throw a checked exception. * *

The {@link Executors} class contains utility methods to * convert from other common forms to {@code Callable} classes. * * @see Executor * @since 1.5 * @author Doug Lea * @param the result type of method {@code call} */ @FunctionalInterface public interface Callable { /** * Computes a result, or throws an exception if unable to do so. * * @return computed result * @throws Exception if unable to compute a result */ V call() throws Exception; /** * Computes this task's result with a borrowed monitor scoped to this call. * The no-argument {@link #call()} remains the sole abstract method. * * @param monitor the borrowed monitor to bind during this call * @return the computed result * @throws NullPointerException if {@code monitor} is {@code null} * @throws CancellationException if cancellation is observed before or * after this call * @throws Exception if this task cannot compute a result */ default V call(ProgressMonitor monitor) throws Exception { return ProgressMonitors.call(this, monitor); } }

See the GNU General Public License * version 2 for more details (a copy is included in the LICENSE file that * accompanied this code). * * You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License version * 2 along with this work; if not, write to the Free Software Foundation, * Inc., 51 Franklin St, Fifth Floor, Boston, MA 02110-1301 USA. * * Please contact Oracle, 500 Oracle Parkway, Redwood Shores, CA 94065 USA * or visit www.oracle.com if you need additional information or have any * questions. */ /* * This file is available under and governed by the GNU General Public * License version 2 only, as published by the Free Software Foundation. * However, the following notice accompanied the original version of this * file: * * Written by Doug Lea with assistance from members of JCP JSR-166 * Expert Group and released to the public domain, as explained at * http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/ */ package java.util.concurrent; import java.util.Collection; import java.util.List; /** * An {@link Executor} that provides methods to manage termination and * methods that can produce a {@link Future} for tracking progress of * one or more asynchronous tasks. * *

An {@code ExecutorService} can be shut down, which will cause * it to reject new tasks. Two different methods are provided for * shutting down an {@code ExecutorService}. The {@link #shutdown} * method will allow previously submitted tasks to execute before * terminating, while the {@link #shutdownNow} method prevents waiting * tasks from starting and attempts to stop currently executing tasks. * Upon termination, an executor has no tasks actively executing, no * tasks awaiting execution, and no new tasks can be submitted. An * unused {@code ExecutorService} should be shut down to allow * reclamation of its resources. * *

Method {@code submit} extends base method {@link * Executor#execute(Runnable)} by creating and returning a {@link Future} * that can be used to cancel execution and/or wait for completion. * Methods {@code invokeAny} and {@code invokeAll} perform the most * commonly useful forms of bulk execution, executing a collection of * tasks and then waiting for at least one, or all, to * complete. (Class {@link ExecutorCompletionService} can be used to * write customized variants of these methods.) * *

The {@link Executors} class provides factory methods for the * executor services provided in this package. * *

Usage Examples

* * Here is a sketch of a network service in which threads in a thread * pool service incoming requests. It uses the preconfigured {@link * Executors#newFixedThreadPool} factory method: * * 
 {@code
 * class NetworkService implements Runnable {
 *   private final ServerSocket serverSocket;
 *   private final ExecutorService pool;
 *
 *   public NetworkService(int port, int poolSize)
 *       throws IOException {
 *     serverSocket = new ServerSocket(port);
 *     pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(poolSize);
 *   }
 *
 *   public void run() { // run the service
 *     try {
 *       for (;;) {
 *         pool.execute(new Handler(serverSocket.accept()));
 *       }
 *     } catch (IOException ex) {
 *       pool.shutdown();
 *     }
 *   }
 * }
 *
 * class Handler implements Runnable {
 *   private final Socket socket;
 *   Handler(Socket socket) { this.socket = socket; }
 *   public void run() {
 *     // read and service request on socket
 *   }
 * }}
* * An {@code ExecutorService} may also be established and closed * (shutdown, blocking until terminated) as follows; illustrating with * a different {@code Executors} factory method: * * 
 {@code
 * try (ExecutorService e =  Executors.newWorkStealingPool()) {
 *   // submit or execute many tasks with e ...
 * }}
* * Further customization is also possible. For example, the following * method shuts down an {@code ExecutorService} in two phases, first * by calling {@code shutdown} to reject incoming tasks, and then * calling {@code shutdownNow}, if necessary, to cancel any lingering * tasks: * * 
 {@code
 * void shutdownAndAwaitTermination(ExecutorService pool) {
 *   pool.shutdown(); // Disable new tasks from being submitted
 *   try {
 *     // Wait a while for existing tasks to terminate
 *     if (!pool.awaitTermination(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS)) {
 *       pool.shutdownNow(); // Cancel currently executing tasks
 *       // Wait a while for tasks to respond to being cancelled
 *       if (!pool.awaitTermination(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS))
 *           System.err.println("Pool did not terminate");
 *     }
 *   } catch (InterruptedException ex) {
 *     // (Re-)Cancel if current thread also interrupted
 *     pool.shutdownNow();
 *     // Preserve interrupt status
 *     Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
 *   }
 * }}
* *

Memory consistency effects: Actions in a thread prior to the * submission of a {@code Runnable} or {@code Callable} task to an * {@code ExecutorService} * happen-before * any actions taken by that task, which in turn happen-before the * result is retrieved via {@code Future.get()}. * * @since 1.5 * @author Doug Lea */ public interface ExecutorService extends Executor, AutoCloseable { /** * Initiates an orderly shutdown in which previously submitted * tasks are executed, but no new tasks will be accepted. * Invocation has no additional effect if already shut down. * *

This method does not wait for previously submitted tasks to * complete execution. Use {@link #awaitTermination awaitTermination} * to do that. * * @throws SecurityException if a security manager exists and * shutting down this ExecutorService may manipulate * threads that the caller is not permitted to modify * because it does not hold {@link * java.lang.RuntimePermission}{@code ("modifyThread")}, * or the security manager's {@code checkAccess} method * denies access. */ void shutdown(); /** * Attempts to stop all actively executing tasks, halts the * processing of waiting tasks, and returns a list of the tasks * that were awaiting execution. * *

This method does not wait for actively executing tasks to * terminate. Use {@link #awaitTermination awaitTermination} to * do that. * *

There are no guarantees beyond best-effort attempts to stop * processing actively executing tasks. For example, typical * implementations will cancel via {@link Thread#interrupt}, so any * task that fails to respond to interrupts may never terminate. * * @return list of tasks that never commenced execution * @throws SecurityException if a security manager exists and * shutting down this ExecutorService may manipulate * threads that the caller is not permitted to modify * because it does not hold {@link * java.lang.RuntimePermission}{@code ("modifyThread")}, * or the security manager's {@code checkAccess} method * denies access. */ List shutdownNow(); /** * Returns {@code true} if this executor has been shut down. * * @return {@code true} if this executor has been shut down */ boolean isShutdown(); /** * Returns {@code true} if all tasks have completed following shut down. * Note that {@code isTerminated} is never {@code true} unless * either {@code shutdown} or {@code shutdownNow} was called first. * * @return {@code true} if all tasks have completed following shut down */ boolean isTerminated(); /** * Blocks until all tasks have completed execution after a shutdown * request, or the timeout occurs, or the current thread is * interrupted, whichever happens first. * * @param timeout the maximum time to wait * @param unit the time unit of the timeout argument * @return {@code true} if this executor terminated and * {@code false} if the timeout elapsed before termination * @throws InterruptedException if interrupted while waiting */ boolean awaitTermination(long timeout, TimeUnit unit) throws InterruptedException; /** * Submits a value-returning task for execution and returns a * Future representing the pending results of the task. The * Future's {@code get} method will return the task's result upon * successful completion. * *

* If you would like to immediately block waiting * for a task, you can use constructions of the form * {@code result = exec.submit(aCallable).get();} * *

Note: The {@link Executors} class includes a set of methods * that can convert some other common closure-like objects, * for example, {@link java.security.PrivilegedAction} to * {@link Callable} form so they can be submitted. * * @param task the task to submit * @param the type of the task's result * @return a Future representing pending completion of the task * @throws RejectedExecutionException if the task cannot be * scheduled for execution * @throws NullPointerException if the task is null */ Future submit(Callable task); /** * Submits a Runnable task for execution and returns a Future * representing that task. The Future's {@code get} method will * return the given result upon successful completion. * * @param task the task to submit * @param result the result to return * @param the type of the result * @return a Future representing pending completion of the task * @throws RejectedExecutionException if the task cannot be * scheduled for execution * @throws NullPointerException if the task is null */ Future submit(Runnable task, T result); /** * Submits a Runnable task for execution and returns a Future * representing that task. The Future's {@code get} method will * return {@code null} upon successful completion. * * @param task the task to submit * @return a Future representing pending completion of the task * @throws RejectedExecutionException if the task cannot be * scheduled for execution * @throws NullPointerException if the task is null */ Future submit(Runnable task); /** * Executes the given tasks, returning a list of Futures holding * their status and results when all complete. * {@link Future#isDone} is {@code true} for each * element of the returned list. * Note that a completed task could have * terminated either normally or by throwing an exception. * The results of this method are undefined if the given * collection is modified while this operation is in progress. * * @param tasks the collection of tasks * @param the type of the values returned from the tasks * @return a list of Futures representing the tasks, in the same * sequential order as produced by the iterator for the * given task list, each of which has completed * @throws InterruptedException if interrupted while waiting, in * which case unfinished tasks are cancelled * @throws NullPointerException if tasks or any of its elements are {@code null} * @throws RejectedExecutionException if any task cannot be * scheduled for execution */ List> invokeAll(Collection> tasks) throws InterruptedException; /** * Executes the given tasks, returning a list of Futures holding * their status and results * when all complete or the timeout expires, whichever happens first. * {@link Future#isDone} is {@code true} for each * element of the returned list. * Upon return, tasks that have not completed are cancelled. * Note that a completed task could have * terminated either normally or by throwing an exception. * The results of this method are undefined if the given * collection is modified while this operation is in progress. * * @param tasks the collection of tasks * @param timeout the maximum time to wait * @param unit the time unit of the timeout argument * @param the type of the values returned from the tasks * @return a list of Futures representing the tasks, in the same * sequential order as produced by the iterator for the * given task list. If the operation did not time out, * each task will have completed. If it did time out, some * of these tasks will not have completed. * @throws InterruptedException if interrupted while waiting, in * which case unfinished tasks are cancelled * @throws NullPointerException if tasks, any of its elements, or * unit are {@code null} * @throws RejectedExecutionException if any task cannot be scheduled * for execution */ List> invokeAll(Collection> tasks, long timeout, TimeUnit unit) throws InterruptedException; /** * Executes the given tasks, returning the result * of one that has completed successfully (i.e., without throwing * an exception), if any do. Upon normal or exceptional return, * tasks that have not completed are cancelled. * The results of this method are undefined if the given * collection is modified while this operation is in progress. * * @param tasks the collection of tasks * @param the type of the values returned from the tasks * @return the result returned by one of the tasks * @throws InterruptedException if interrupted while waiting * @throws NullPointerException if tasks or any element task * subject to execution is {@code null} * @throws IllegalArgumentException if tasks is empty * @throws ExecutionException if no task successfully completes * @throws RejectedExecutionException if tasks cannot be scheduled * for execution */ T invokeAny(Collection> tasks) throws InterruptedException, ExecutionException; /** * Executes the given tasks, returning the result * of one that has completed successfully (i.e., without throwing * an exception), if any do before the given timeout elapses. * Upon normal or exceptional return, tasks that have not * completed are cancelled. * The results of this method are undefined if the given * collection is modified while this operation is in progress. * * @param tasks the collection of tasks * @param timeout the maximum time to wait * @param unit the time unit of the timeout argument * @param the type of the values returned from the tasks * @return the result returned by one of the tasks * @throws InterruptedException if interrupted while waiting * @throws NullPointerException if tasks, or unit, or any element * task subject to execution is {@code null} * @throws TimeoutException if the given timeout elapses before * any task successfully completes * @throws ExecutionException if no task successfully completes * @throws RejectedExecutionException if tasks cannot be scheduled * for execution */ T invokeAny(Collection> tasks, long timeout, TimeUnit unit) throws InterruptedException, ExecutionException, TimeoutException; /** * Initiates an orderly shutdown in which previously submitted tasks are * executed, but no new tasks will be accepted. This method waits until all * tasks have completed execution and the executor has terminated. * *

If interrupted while waiting, this method stops all executing tasks as * if by invoking {@link #shutdownNow()}. It then continues to wait until all * actively executing tasks have completed. Tasks that were awaiting * execution are not executed. The interrupt status will be re-asserted * before this method returns. * *

If already terminated, invoking this method has no effect. * * @implSpec * The default implementation invokes {@code shutdown()} and waits for tasks * to complete execution with {@code awaitTermination}. * * @throws SecurityException if a security manager exists and * shutting down this ExecutorService may manipulate * threads that the caller is not permitted to modify * because it does not hold {@link * java.lang.RuntimePermission}{@code ("modifyThread")}, * or the security manager's {@code checkAccess} method * denies access. * @since 19 */ @Override default void close() { boolean terminated = isTerminated(); if (!terminated) { shutdown(); boolean interrupted = false; while (!terminated) { try { terminated = awaitTermination(1L, TimeUnit.DAYS); } catch (InterruptedException e) { if (!interrupted) { shutdownNow(); interrupted = true; } } } if (interrupted) { Thread.currentThread().interrupt(); } } } /** * Run a checked task with an explicitly borrowed progress monitor. * Future cancellation and cooperative monitor cancellation remain distinct. * The monitor is bound during execution and is not completed by this task. * * @param the task's result type * @param task the task to submit * @param monitor the borrowed monitor to bind during the task * @return a future representing pending completion of the task * @throws NullPointerException if {@code task} or {@code monitor} is null * @throws RejectedExecutionException if the task cannot be scheduled */ default Future submitMonitored(Callable task, ProgressMonitor monitor) { java.util.Objects.requireNonNull(task, "task"); java.util.Objects.requireNonNull(monitor, "monitor"); return submit((Callable) () -> ProgressMonitors.call(task, monitor)); } /** * Submits a runnable with a borrowed monitor scoped to its execution. * Avoids overloading {@code submit(Runnable,T)}, which would change * overload resolution. Completion does not finish the borrowed monitor. * * @param task the task to submit * @param monitor the borrowed monitor to bind during the task * @return a future whose successful completion result is {@code null} * @throws NullPointerException if {@code task} or {@code monitor} is null * @throws RejectedExecutionException if the task cannot be scheduled */ default Future submitMonitored(Runnable task, ProgressMonitor monitor) { java.util.Objects.requireNonNull(task, "task"); java.util.Objects.requireNonNull(monitor, "monitor"); return submit((Runnable) () -> ProgressMonitors.run(task, monitor)); } }

# ProgressJob: a separate Callable-oriented API candidate

`java.util.concurrent.ProgressJob<S>` gives JDK-owned subclasses a protected
`run(ProgressMonitor)` hook that returns the caller's result type. Its two final
entry points delegate directly to the existing `MonitoredCallable` template and
the protected body. It introduces no task state, scheduler, status conversion,
native code, or dependency from `java.base` to a framework.

This is a new public API candidate. `RECEIVING-MAP.json` records
`PENDING_FULL_IMAGE_API_REVIEW_AND_ORDERED_PHASE`; the active STRING phase and the
existing universal `Object.toAdapter` compatibility HOLD remain unchanged. A
passing bounded test does not advance either gate or establish full Eclipse Job
or Synexia context parity. This packet is separate from the frozen runtime repairs.

## Result and cancellation contracts

The caller can choose `S` as the real Eclipse `IStatus`, the distinct Synexia
`IJobResult`, or another result type. Successful values, including null, are
returned unchanged. The existing template propagates a body exception unchanged
and throws `CancellationException` if its monitor checks observe cancellation.
It can therefore reject a returned `Status.CANCEL_STATUS` when the monitor was
canceled. Eclipse Job's scheduler, `ASYNC_FINISH`, non-null IStatus contract,
listeners and result conversion are not supplied by this class.

`call()` uses the executing thread's current monitor. Inherited `call(monitor)`
binds an explicit borrowed monitor and restores the prior scope. Direct
`callMonitored(monitor)` is the body entry point: it passes its argument unchanged
and does not bind a scope or check cancellation. Neither path completes a
borrowed monitor. The class has no fields; subclasses and monitors still own the
thread-safety contract of their state.

## Using the existing executor owners

For an ordinary Executor, bind inside a FutureTask's Callable:

```java
FutureTask<IStatus> future = new FutureTask<>(() -> job.call(monitor));
executor.execute(future);
IStatus result = future.get();
```

The actual Eclipse type belongs to the application class path. A pre-cancellation
exception is recorded as exceptional completion by FutureTask; `get()` throws an
`ExecutionException` whose cause is that exception. This is not `Future.cancel`:
`isDone()` is true and `isCancelled()` is false. A checked body exception is the
unchanged cause of `ExecutionException`. The existing
`executorService.submitMonitored(job, monitor)` also binds inside its submitted
Callable. Ordinary `submit(job)` continues to use the worker's current monitor
and does not capture the submitting thread's scope.

An outer `executor.execute(future, monitor)` can reject a canceled monitor before
`FutureTask.run()` executes and leave that future pending. The regression witness
retains this counterexample and uses the inner binding above for the supported
adapter. No new scheduler is needed.

This new base is Callable-oriented. Its value-returning `run(ProgressMonitor)`
conflicts with Runnable's already published void progress overload, so a subclass
cannot also implement Runnable. The negative source witness records this
limitation. Separate old classes that already implement Runnable and Callable
are compiled with an unmodified stock JDK and exercised unchanged as finite
compatibility witnesses; they are not evidence of universal source compatibility.

## Reproduction and evidence boundaries

After receiving, run `verify_progress_job.py --baseline-root <repair-source-tree>

--eclipse-dir <pinned-eclipse-inputs> --output <new-proof-directory>`. The exact

# ProgressJob: a separate Callable-oriented API candidate

`java.util.concurrent.ProgressJob<S>` gives JDK-owned subclasses a protected
`run(ProgressMonitor)` hook that returns the caller's result type. Its two final
entry points delegate directly to the existing `MonitoredCallable` template and
the protected body. It introduces no task state, scheduler, status conversion,
native code, or dependency from `java.base` to a framework.

This is a new public API candidate. `RECEIVING-MAP.json` records
`PENDING_FULL_IMAGE_API_REVIEW_AND_ORDERED_PHASE`; the active STRING phase and the
existing universal `Object.toAdapter` compatibility HOLD remain unchanged. A
passing bounded test does not advance either gate or establish full Eclipse Job
or Synexia context parity. This packet is separate from the frozen runtime repairs.

## Result and cancellation contracts

The caller can choose `S` as the real Eclipse `IStatus`, the distinct Synexia
`IJobResult`, or another result type. Successful values, including null, are
returned unchanged. The existing template propagates a body exception unchanged
and throws `CancellationException` if its monitor checks observe cancellation.
It can therefore reject a returned `Status.CANCEL_STATUS` when the monitor was
canceled. Eclipse Job's scheduler, `ASYNC_FINISH`, non-null IStatus contract,
listeners and result conversion are not supplied by this class.

`call()` uses the executing thread's current monitor. Inherited `call(monitor)`
binds an explicit borrowed monitor and restores the prior scope. Direct
`callMonitored(monitor)` is the body entry point: it passes its argument unchanged
and does not bind a scope or check cancellation. Neither path completes a
borrowed monitor. The class has no fields; subclasses and monitors still own the
thread-safety contract of their state.

## Using the existing executor owners

For an ordinary Executor, bind inside a FutureTask's Callable:

```java
FutureTask<IStatus> future = new FutureTask<>(() -> job.call(monitor));
executor.execute(future);
IStatus result = future.get();
```

The actual Eclipse type belongs to the application class path. A pre-cancellation
exception is recorded as exceptional completion by FutureTask; `get()` throws an
`ExecutionException` whose cause is that exception. This is not `Future.cancel`:
`isDone()` is true and `isCancelled()` is false. A checked body exception is the
unchanged cause of `ExecutionException`. The existing
`executorService.submitMonitored(job, monitor)` also binds inside its submitted
Callable. Ordinary `submit(job)` continues to use the worker's current monitor
and does not capture the submitting thread's scope.

An outer `executor.execute(future, monitor)` can reject a canceled monitor before
`FutureTask.run()` executes and leave that future pending. The regression witness
retains this counterexample and uses the inner binding above for the supported
adapter. No new scheduler is needed.

This new base is Callable-oriented. Its value-returning `run(ProgressMonitor)`
conflicts with Runnable's already published void progress overload, so a subclass
cannot also implement Runnable. The negative source witness records this
limitation. Separate old classes that already implement Runnable and Callable
are compiled with an unmodified stock JDK and exercised unchanged as finite
compatibility witnesses; they are not evidence of universal source compatibility.

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import traceback


PREFIX = "m3/runtime-integration/progress-job-20261018"
OWNER = "src/java.base/share/classes/java/util/concurrent/ProgressJob.java"
JDK_TEST = "test/jdk/java/util/concurrent/ProgressJob/M3ProgressJob.java"
JDK_FLAGS = ["-g:none", "-proc:none", "-Xlint:all", "-Xlint:-this-escape", "-Werror",
             "-Xdoclint:all/protected", "-Xdoclint/package:java.*,javax.*"]
CLIENT_FLAGS = ["-g:none", "-proc:none", "-Xlint:all", "-Werror"]


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def class_tree(root):
    return {p.relative_to(root).as_posix(): sha(p) for p in sorted(root.rglob("*.class"))}


def copy(source, target):
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copyfile(source, target)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    for name in ("baseline-root", "candidate", "stock-jdk", "m3-jdk", "eclipse-dir", "output"):
        parser.add_argument("--" + name, type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.output = args.output.resolve()
    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    observations = []
    receipt = {"schema": "M3_PROGRESS_JOB_BEHAVIOR_PROOF_V1", "result": "RUNNING",
               "product_sources_written": False, "jdk_images_modified": False,
               "full_image_with_new_api": "NOT_RUN_PATCHED_IMAGE_ONLY",
               "public_api_admission": "PENDING_FULL_IMAGE_API_REVIEW_AND_ORDERED_PHASE",
               "Object_universal_compatibility": "HOLD_UNCHANGED", "phase": "STRING_UNCHANGED",
               "commands": observations}

    def run(label, command, expected_success=True, quiet_success=False, timeout=120):
        result = subprocess.run([str(value) for value in command], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        stdout = args.output / (label + ".stdout.log")
        stderr = args.output / (label + ".stderr.log")
        stdout.write_text(result.stdout)
        stderr.write_text(result.stderr)
        observations.append({"label": label, "command": [str(value) for value in command],
                             "exit": result.returncode, "expected_success": expected_success,
                             "stdout_sha256": sha(stdout), "stderr_sha256": sha(stderr)})
        if (result.returncode == 0) != expected_success:
            raise ValueError("unexpected result: " + label + "\n" + result.stdout + result.stderr)
        if quiet_success and (result.stdout.strip() or result.stderr.strip()):
            raise ValueError("strict compile emitted output: " + label + "\n" + result.stdout + result.stderr)
        return result.stdout, result.stderr

    try:
        review_path = args.candidate / PREFIX / "DONOR-REVIEW.json"
        review = json.loads(review_path.read_text())
        if sha(args.candidate / OWNER) != review["product_source_sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("received ProgressJob differs from reviewed owner")
        receipt["review_sha256"] = sha(review_path)
        receipt["source_sha256"] = review["product_source_sha256"]
        sources = args.output / "stock-source"
        source_paths = []
        for entry in review["current_owner_dependencies"]:
            source = args.baseline_root / entry["path"]
            if sha(source) != entry["sha256"]:
                raise ValueError("existing owner drift: " + entry["path"])
            target = sources / entry["path"]
            copy(source, target)
            source_paths.append(target)
        if len(source_paths) != 7:
            raise ValueError("expected exact seven-source dependency closure")
        owner_copy = sources / OWNER
        copy(args.candidate / OWNER, owner_copy)
        source_paths.append(owner_copy)
        receipt["existing_dependencies"] = review["current_owner_dependencies"]
        artifacts = review["eclipse_release_inputs"]["files"]
        for entry in artifacts:
            if sha(args.eclipse_dir / entry["file"]) != entry["sha256"]:
                raise ValueError("external artifact drift: " + entry["file"])
        jars = [args.eclipse_dir / "org.eclipse.equinox.common-3.21.0.jar",
                args.eclipse_dir / "org.eclipse.osgi-3.24.300.jar"]
        eclipse_classpath = ":".join(str(path.resolve()) for path in jars)
        receipt["external_eclipse_jars"] = [{"path": path.name, "sha256": sha(path)} for path in jars]
        stock_java = (args.stock_jdk / "bin/java").resolve()
        stock_javac = (args.stock_jdk / "bin/javac").resolve()
        image_java = (args.m3_jdk / "bin/java").resolve()
        image_javac = (args.m3_jdk / "bin/javac").resolve()
        for label, executable in (("stock-javac-version", stock_javac), ("image-javac-version", image_javac)):
            stdout, stderr = run(label, [executable, "-version"])
            if not (stdout + stderr).strip().startswith("javac 21"):
                raise ValueError("requires actual Java 21 compiler")
        run("stock-java-version", [stock_java, "-version"])
        run("image-java-version", [image_java, "-version"])
        receipt["toolchain_sha256"] = {str(path): sha(path) for path in (stock_java, stock_javac, image_java, image_javac)}
        stock_classes = args.output / "stock-patch-classes"
        image_classes = args.output / "image-new-class"
        stock_classes.mkdir()
        image_classes.mkdir()
        patch_source = (sources / "src/java.base/share/classes").resolve()
        run("stock-strict-api", [stock_javac, *JDK_FLAGS, "--patch-module", "java.base=" + str(patch_source),
                                  "-d", stock_classes, *source_paths], quiet_success=True)
        image_source = args.output / "image-new-source/java/util/concurrent/ProgressJob.java"
        copy(args.candidate / OWNER, image_source)
        run("image-strict-api", [image_javac, *JDK_FLAGS, "--patch-module", "java.base=" + str(image_source.parents[3]),
                                  "-d", image_classes, image_source], quiet_success=True)
        new_class = "java/util/concurrent/ProgressJob.class"
        if class_tree(image_classes) != {new_class: sha(stock_classes / new_class)}:
            raise ValueError("new class differs between stock closure and existing M3 image compiles")
        receipt["new_class_sha256"] = sha(image_classes / new_class)
        receipt["stock_patch_classes"] = class_tree(stock_classes)
        run("new-class-bytecode", [args.stock_jdk / "bin/javap", "-p", "-c", "-s", "-verbose", image_classes / new_class])
        clients = args.output / "new-client-classes"
        clients.mkdir()
        run("strict-core-test", [stock_javac, *CLIENT_FLAGS, "--patch-module", "java.base=" + str(stock_classes),
                                 "-d", clients, args.candidate / JDK_TEST], quiet_success=True)
        eclipse_source = args.candidate / PREFIX / "src/test/java/EclipseStatusIdentity.java"
        run("strict-eclipse-test", [stock_javac, *CLIENT_FLAGS, "--patch-module", "java.base=" + str(stock_classes),
                                    "-classpath", eclipse_classpath, "-d", clients, eclipse_source], quiet_success=True)
        old_source = args.candidate / PREFIX / "src/test/java/OldCallableClient.java"
        old_classes = args.output / "frozen-stock-client"
        old_classes.mkdir()
        run("stock-old-client-compile", [stock_javac, *CLIENT_FLAGS, "-d", old_classes, old_source], quiet_success=True)
        frozen_classes = class_tree(old_classes)
        if len(frozen_classes) != 3:
            raise ValueError("unexpected frozen old client closure")
        old_new_classes = args.output / "recompiled-old-client"
        old_new_classes.mkdir()
        run("patched-old-client-source", [stock_javac, *CLIENT_FLAGS, "--patch-module", "java.base=" + str(stock_classes),
                                           "-d", old_new_classes, old_source], quiet_success=True)
        if class_tree(old_new_classes) != frozen_classes:
            raise ValueError("finite old client produces different bytes with added API")
        negative = args.output / "negative-source/ProgressJobRunnableConflict.java"
        copy(args.candidate / PREFIX / "src/test/resources/ProgressJobRunnableConflict.java.txt", negative)
        negative_classes = args.output / "negative-classes"
        negative_classes.mkdir()
        stdout, stderr = run("new-runnable-subclass-conflict", [stock_javac, *CLIENT_FLAGS, "-XDrawDiagnostics",
                                "--patch-module", "java.base=" + str(stock_classes), "-d", negative_classes, negative],
                               expected_success=False)
        keys = re.findall(r"compiler\.err\.[a-zA-Z0-9_.]+", stderr)
        if not keys or not any(key in ("compiler.err.override.incompatible.ret", "compiler.err.override.weaker.access") for key in keys):
            raise ValueError("expected new Runnable return/access conflict was not observed: " + stderr)
        if any("cant.resolve" in key for key in keys):
            raise ValueError("negative witness failed due to unavailable API")
        receipt["new_runnable_subclass"] = {"result": "EXPECTED_CONFLICT", "diagnostic_keys": keys,
                                            "old_dual_clients": "SEPARATE_FINITE_POSITIVE_WITNESS"}
        stdout, _ = run("stock-old-client-run", [stock_java, "-Xmx256m", "-ea", "-classpath", old_classes, "OldCallableClient"])
        if "PASS old Callable" not in stdout:
            raise ValueError("stock old client did not execute")
        counts = {}
        for label, java, patch in (("stock-patched", stock_java, stock_classes), ("m3-image-patched", image_java, image_classes)):
            runtime = [java, "-Xmx256m", "-ea", "-Xcheck:jni", "--patch-module", "java.base=" + str(patch)]
            stdout, _ = run(label + "-old-binary", [*runtime, "-classpath", old_classes, "OldCallableClient"])
            if "PASS old Callable" not in stdout:
                raise ValueError("frozen old binary did not execute")
            stdout, _ = run(label + "-core", [*runtime, "-classpath", clients, "M3ProgressJob"])
            match = re.search(r"PASS ProgressJob checks=(\d+)", stdout)
            if match is None:
                raise ValueError("core witness did not execute")
            core_count = int(match.group(1))
            stdout, _ = run(label + "-eclipse", [*runtime, "-classpath", str(clients) + ":" + eclipse_classpath, "EclipseStatusIdentity"])
            match = re.search(r"PASS real Eclipse IStatus/Status/MultiStatus checks=(\d+)", stdout)
            if match is None:
                raise ValueError("actual Eclipse status witness did not execute")
            counts[label] = {"core_checks": core_count, "real_eclipse_checks": int(match.group(1))}
        if counts["stock-patched"] != counts["m3-image-patched"]:
            raise ValueError("runtime witness counts differ")
        if class_tree(old_classes) != frozen_classes:
            raise ValueError("frozen old client class bytes changed during execution")
        receipt["frozen_stock_client_classes"] = frozen_classes
        receipt["new_client_classes"] = class_tree(clients)
        receipt["checks"] = counts
        receipt["synexia_result_runtime"] = "NOT_RUN: exact IJobResult/AbstractJob/IAdaptable source review only; no stubbed substitute or whole context closure claim"
        receipt["result"] = "PASS"
    except Exception as error:
        receipt["result"] = "FAIL"
        receipt["failure"] = str(error)
        (args.output / "failure.txt").write_text(traceback.format_exc())
        raise
    finally:
        (args.output / "receipt.json").write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2) + "\n")
    print("PASS", json.dumps(receipt["checks"], sort_keys=True), "; new API pending; full new image not run; existing HOLD unchanged")

# ProgressJob: a separate Callable-oriented API candidate

`java.util.concurrent.ProgressJob<S>` gives JDK-owned subclasses a protected
`run(ProgressMonitor)` hook that returns the caller's result type. Its two final
entry points delegate directly to the existing `MonitoredCallable` template and
the protected body. It introduces no task state, scheduler, status conversion,
native code, or dependency from `java.base` to a framework.

This is a new public API candidate. `RECEIVING-MAP.json` records
`PENDING_FULL_IMAGE_API_REVIEW_AND_ORDERED_PHASE`; the active STRING phase and the
existing universal `Object.toAdapter` compatibility HOLD remain unchanged. A
passing bounded test does not advance either gate or establish full Eclipse Job
or Synexia context parity. This packet is separate from the frozen runtime repairs.

## Result and cancellation contracts

The caller can choose `S` as the real Eclipse `IStatus`, the distinct Synexia
`IJobResult`, or another result type. Successful values, including null, are
returned unchanged. The existing template propagates a body exception unchanged
and throws `CancellationException` if its monitor checks observe cancellation.
It can therefore reject a returned `Status.CANCEL_STATUS` when the monitor was
canceled. Eclipse Job's scheduler, `ASYNC_FINISH`, non-null IStatus contract,
listeners and result conversion are not supplied by this class.

`call()` uses the executing thread's current monitor. Inherited `call(monitor)`
binds an explicit borrowed monitor and restores the prior scope. Direct
`callMonitored(monitor)` is the body entry point: it passes its argument unchanged
and does not bind a scope or check cancellation. Neither path completes a
borrowed monitor. The class has no fields; subclasses and monitors still own the
thread-safety contract of their state.

## Using the existing executor owners

For an ordinary Executor, bind inside a FutureTask's Callable:

```java
FutureTask<IStatus> future = new FutureTask<>(() -> job.call(monitor));
executor.execute(future);
IStatus result = future.get();
```

The actual Eclipse type belongs to the application class path. A pre-cancellation
exception is recorded as exceptional completion by FutureTask; `get()` throws an
`ExecutionException` whose cause is that exception. This is not `Future.cancel`:
`isDone()` is true and `isCancelled()` is false. A checked body exception is the
unchanged cause of `ExecutionException`. The existing
`executorService.submitMonitored(job, monitor)` also binds inside its submitted
Callable. Ordinary `submit(job)` continues to use the worker's current monitor
and does not capture the submitting thread's scope.

An outer `executor.execute(future, monitor)` can reject a canceled monitor before
`FutureTask.run()` executes and leave that future pending. The regression witness
retains this counterexample and uses the inner binding above for the supported
adapter. No new scheduler is needed.

This new base is Callable-oriented. Its value-returning `run(ProgressMonitor)`
conflicts with Runnable's already published void progress overload, so a subclass
cannot also implement Runnable. The negative source witness records this
limitation. Separate old classes that already implement Runnable and Callable
are compiled with an unmodified stock JDK and exercised unchanged as finite
compatibility witnesses; they are not evidence of universal source compatibility.

# ProgressJob: a separate Callable-oriented API candidate

`java.util.concurrent.ProgressJob<S>` gives JDK-owned subclasses a protected
`run(ProgressMonitor)` hook that returns the caller's result type. Its two final
entry points delegate directly to the existing `MonitoredCallable` template and
the protected body. It introduces no task state, scheduler, status conversion,
native code, or dependency from `java.base` to a framework.

This is a new public API candidate. `RECEIVING-MAP.json` records
`PENDING_FULL_IMAGE_API_REVIEW_AND_ORDERED_PHASE`; the active STRING phase and the
existing universal `Object.toAdapter` compatibility HOLD remain unchanged. A
passing bounded test does not advance either gate or establish full Eclipse Job
or Synexia context parity. This packet is separate from the frozen runtime repairs.

## Result and cancellation contracts

The caller can choose `S` as the real Eclipse `IStatus`, the distinct Synexia
`IJobResult`, or another result type. Successful values, including null, are
returned unchanged. The existing template propagates a body exception unchanged
and throws `CancellationException` if its monitor checks observe cancellation.
It can therefore reject a returned `Status.CANCEL_STATUS` when the monitor was
canceled. Eclipse Job's scheduler, `ASYNC_FINISH`, non-null IStatus contract,
listeners and result conversion are not supplied by this class.

`call()` uses the executing thread's current monitor. Inherited `call(monitor)`
binds an explicit borrowed monitor and restores the prior scope. Direct
`callMonitored(monitor)` is the body entry point: it passes its argument unchanged
and does not bind a scope or check cancellation. Neither path completes a
borrowed monitor. The class has no fields; subclasses and monitors still own the
thread-safety contract of their state.

## Using the existing executor owners

For an ordinary Executor, bind inside a FutureTask's Callable:

```java
FutureTask<IStatus> future = new FutureTask<>(() -> job.call(monitor));
executor.execute(future);
IStatus result = future.get();
```

The actual Eclipse type belongs to the application class path. A pre-cancellation
exception is recorded as exceptional completion by FutureTask; `get()` throws an
`ExecutionException` whose cause is that exception. This is not `Future.cancel`:
`isDone()` is true and `isCancelled()` is false. A checked body exception is the
unchanged cause of `ExecutionException`. The existing
`executorService.submitMonitored(job, monitor)` also binds inside its submitted
Callable. Ordinary `submit(job)` continues to use the worker's current monitor
and does not capture the submitting thread's scope.

An outer `executor.execute(future, monitor)` can reject a canceled monitor before
`FutureTask.run()` executes and leave that future pending. The regression witness
retains this counterexample and uses the inner binding above for the supported
adapter. No new scheduler is needed.

This new base is Callable-oriented. Its value-returning `run(ProgressMonitor)`
conflicts with Runnable's already published void progress overload, so a subclass
cannot also implement Runnable. The negative source witness records this
limitation. Separate old classes that already implement Runnable and Callable
are compiled with an unmodified stock JDK and exercised unchanged as finite
compatibility witnesses; they are not evidence of universal source compatibility.

+# ProgressJob: a separate Callable-oriented API candidate
+
+`java.util.concurrent.ProgressJob<S>` gives JDK-owned subclasses a protected
+`run(ProgressMonitor)` hook that returns the caller's result type. Its two final
+entry points delegate directly to the existing `MonitoredCallable` template and
+the protected body. It introduces no task state, scheduler, status conversion,
+native code, or dependency from `java.base` to a framework.
+
+This is a new public API candidate. `RECEIVING-MAP.json` records
+`PENDING_FULL_IMAGE_API_REVIEW_AND_ORDERED_PHASE`; the active STRING phase and the
+existing universal `Object.toAdapter` compatibility HOLD remain unchanged. A
+passing bounded test does not advance either gate or establish full Eclipse Job
+or Synexia context parity. This packet is separate from the frozen runtime repairs.
+
+## Result and cancellation contracts
+
+The caller can choose `S` as the real Eclipse `IStatus`, the distinct Synexia
+`IJobResult`, or another result type. Successful values, including null, are
+returned unchanged. The existing template propagates a body exception unchanged
+and throws `CancellationException` if its monitor checks observe cancellation.
+It can therefore reject a returned `Status.CANCEL_STATUS` when the monitor was
+canceled. Eclipse Job's scheduler, `ASYNC_FINISH`, non-null IStatus contract,
+listeners and result conversion are not supplied by this class.
+
+`call()` uses the executing thread's current monitor. Inherited `call(monitor)`
+binds an explicit borrowed monitor and restores the prior scope. Direct
+`callMonitored(monitor)` is the body entry point: it passes its argument unchanged
+and does not bind a scope or check cancellation. Neither path completes a
+borrowed monitor. The class has no fields; subclasses and monitors still own the
+thread-safety contract of their state.
+
+## Using the existing executor owners
+
+For an ordinary Executor, bind inside a FutureTask's Callable:
+
+```java
+FutureTask<IStatus> future = new FutureTask<>(() -> job.call(monitor));
+executor.execute(future);
+IStatus result = future.get();
+```
+
+The actual Eclipse type belongs to the application class path. A pre-cancellation
+exception is recorded as exceptional completion by FutureTask; `get()` throws an
+`ExecutionException` whose cause is that exception. This is not `Future.cancel`:
+`isDone()` is true and `isCancelled()` is false. A checked body exception is the
+unchanged cause of `ExecutionException`. The existing
+`executorService.submitMonitored(job, monitor)` also binds inside its submitted
+Callable. Ordinary `submit(job)` continues to use the worker's current monitor
+and does not capture the submitting thread's scope.
+
+An outer `executor.execute(future, monitor)` can reject a canceled monitor before
+`FutureTask.run()` executes and leave that future pending. The regression witness
+retains this counterexample and uses the inner binding above for the supported
+adapter. No new scheduler is needed.
+
+This new base is Callable-oriented. Its value-returning `run(ProgressMonitor)`
+conflicts with Runnable's already published void progress overload, so a subclass
+cannot also implement Runnable. The negative source witness records this
+limitation. Separate old classes that already implement Runnable and Callable
+are compiled with an unmodified stock JDK and exercised unchanged as finite
+compatibility witnesses; they are not evidence of universal source compatibility.
+
+## Reproduction and evidence boundaries
+
+The reusable Synexia Maven/OpenRewrite host qualifies the sealed dataset
+`m3jdk21-progress-job` with its original five SDK, eight sealer and nine receiver
+cases. Its receiver emits the source, tests, catalogue and mapping. The host and
+recipe engines are unchanged. Target emission must use that qualified receiver;
+never patch generated output to repair a failed transformation.
+
+After receiving, run `verify_progress_job.py --baseline-root <repair-source-tree>
+--candidate <received-tree> --stock-jdk <stock-java21> --m3-jdk <built-m3-java21>
+--eclipse-dir <pinned-eclipse-inputs> --output <new-proof-directory>`. The exact
+existing dependency hashes are in `DONOR-REVIEW.json`. The verifier performs the
+original JDK protected/package doclint and warning-as-error compile, strict
+consumer compiles, frozen stock-client binary runs, core and real Eclipse status
+witnesses on a stock patched JDK and a separately built M3 JDK patched only with
+the new class, and an expected negative Runnable-subclass compile. It records
+commands, source/class identities and outputs. Patching an existing image for
+these tests does not qualify a full new image containing this additive API.
+
+The jtreg core test is
+`test/jdk/java/util/concurrent/ProgressJob/M3ProgressJob.java`. The external Eclipse
+fixture remains under this proof directory and does not make jtreg or java.base
+depend on Eclipse. Real Synexia IJobResult source contracts were reviewed;
+executing its full dependency closure is a separate, unclaimed gate.
+
+`DONOR-REVIEW.json` identifies the exact current JDK, Synexia and Eclipse owners,
+licenses, selection rationale and algorithm-discovery applicability. The new
+java.base class and jtreg test are first-party target-licensed GPL+Classpath
+contributions; recipe/proof tooling is Apache-2.0. Eclipse is an unmodified
+external test dependency and source reference, with no Eclipse implementation
+copied into java.base. No JNI operation changes in this packet.

+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json

+import re
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import traceback
+
+
+PREFIX = "m3/runtime-integration/progress-job-20261018"
+OWNER = "src/java.base/share/classes/java/util/concurrent/ProgressJob.java"

+             "-Xdoclint:all/protected", "-Xdoclint/package:java.*,javax.*"]
+CLIENT_FLAGS = ["-g:none", "-proc:none", "-Xlint:all", "-Werror"]

+
+def sha(path):
+    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+
+
+def class_tree(root):
+    return {p.relative_to(root).as_posix(): sha(p) for p in sorted(root.rglob("*.class"))}
+
+
+def copy(source, target):
+    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    shutil.copyfile(source, target)
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    for name in ("baseline-root", "candidate", "stock-jdk", "m3-jdk", "eclipse-dir", "output"):
+        parser.add_argument("--" + name, type=Path, required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    args.output = args.output.resolve()
+    args.output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
+    observations = []
+    receipt = {"schema": "M3_PROGRESS_JOB_BEHAVIOR_PROOF_V1", "result": "RUNNING",
+               "product_sources_written": False, "jdk_images_modified": False,
+               "full_image_with_new_api": "NOT_RUN_PATCHED_IMAGE_ONLY",
+               "public_api_admission": "PENDING_FULL_IMAGE_API_REVIEW_AND_ORDERED_PHASE",
+               "Object_universal_compatibility": "HOLD_UNCHANGED", "phase": "STRING_UNCHANGED",
+               "commands": observations}
+
+    def run(label, command, expected_success=True, quiet_success=False, timeout=120):
+        result = subprocess.run([str(value) for value in command], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
+        stdout = args.output / (label + ".stdout.log")
+        stderr = args.output / (label + ".stderr.log")
+        stdout.write_text(result.stdout)
+        stderr.write_text(result.stderr)
+        observations.append({"label": label, "command": [str(value) for value in command],
+                             "exit": result.returncode, "expected_success": expected_success,
+                             "stdout_sha256": sha(stdout), "stderr_sha256": sha(stderr)})
+        if (result.returncode == 0) != expected_success:
+            raise ValueError("unexpected result: " + label + "\n" + result.stdout + result.stderr)
+        if quiet_success and (result.stdout.strip() or result.stderr.strip()):
+            raise ValueError("strict compile emitted output: " + label + "\n" + result.stdout + result.stderr)
+        return result.stdout, result.stderr
+
+    try:
+        review_path = args.candidate / PREFIX / "DONOR-REVIEW.json"
+        review = json.loads(review_path.read_text())
+        if sha(args.candidate / OWNER) != review["product_source_sha256"]:
+            raise ValueError("received ProgressJob differs from reviewed owner")
+        receipt["review_sha256"] = sha(review_path)
+        receipt["source_sha256"] = review["product_source_sha256"]
+        sources = args.output / "stock-source"
+        source_paths = []
+        for entry in review["current_owner_dependencies"]:
+            source = args.baseline_root / entry["path"]
+            if sha(source) != entry["sha256"]:
+                raise ValueError("existing owner drift: " + entry["path"])
+            target = sources / entry["path"]
+            copy(source, target)
+            source_paths.append(target)
+        if len(source_paths) != 7:
+            raise ValueError("expected exact seven-source dependency closure")
+        owner_copy = sources / OWNER
+        copy(args.candidate / OWNER, owner_copy)
+        source_paths.append(owner_copy)
+        receipt["existing_dependencies"] = review["current_owner_dependencies"]
+        artifacts = review["eclipse_release_inputs"]["files"]
+        for entry in artifacts:

+        eclipse_classpath = ":".join(str(path.resolve()) for path in jars)
+        receipt["external_eclipse_jars"] = [{"path": path.name, "sha256": sha(path)} for path in jars]
+        stock_java = (args.stock_jdk / "bin/java").resolve()
+        stock_javac = (args.stock_jdk / "bin/javac").resolve()
+        image_java = (args.m3_jdk / "bin/java").resolve()
+        image_javac = (args.m3_jdk / "bin/javac").resolve()
+        for label, executable in (("stock-javac-version", stock_javac), ("image-javac-version", image_javac)):
+            stdout, stderr = run(label, [executable, "-version"])
+            if not (stdout + stderr).strip().startswith("javac 21"):
+                raise ValueError("requires actual Java 21 compiler")

+        run("image-java-version", [image_java, "-version"])
+        receipt["toolchain_sha256"] = {str(path): sha(path) for path in (stock_java, stock_javac, image_java, image_javac)}

+        image_classes = args.output / "image-new-class"
+        stock_classes.mkdir()
+        image_classes.mkdir()
+        patch_source = (sources / "src/java.base/share/classes").resolve()
+        run("stock-strict-api", [stock_javac, *JDK_FLAGS, "--patch-module", "java.base=" + str(patch_source),

+        image_source = args.output / "image-new-source/java/util/concurrent/ProgressJob.java"
+        copy(args.candidate / OWNER, image_source)
+        run("image-strict-api", [image_javac, *JDK_FLAGS, "--patch-module", "java.base=" + str(image_source.parents[3]),
+                                  "-d", image_classes, image_source], quiet_success=True)
+        new_class = "java/util/concurrent/ProgressJob.class"
+        if class_tree(image_classes) != {new_class: sha(stock_classes / new_class)}:
+            raise ValueError("new class differs between stock closure and existing M3 image compiles")

+        receipt["stock_patch_classes"] = class_tree(stock_classes)
+        run("new-class-bytecode", [args.stock_jdk / "bin/javap", "-p", "-c", "-s", "-verbose", image_classes / new_class])
+        clients = args.output / "new-client-classes"
+        clients.mkdir()

+        eclipse_source = args.candidate / PREFIX / "src/test/java/EclipseStatusIdentity.java"
+        run("strict-eclipse-test", [stock_javac, *CLIENT_FLAGS, "--patch-module", "java.base=" + str(stock_classes),
+                                    "-classpath", eclipse_classpath, "-d", clients, eclipse_source], quiet_success=True)
+        old_source = args.candidate / PREFIX / "src/test/java/OldCallableClient.java"
+        old_classes = args.output / "frozen-stock-client"
+        old_classes.mkdir()
+        run("stock-old-client-compile", [stock_javac, *CLIENT_FLAGS, "-d", old_classes, old_source], quiet_success=True)
+        frozen_classes = class_tree(old_classes)
+        if len(frozen_classes) != 3:

+        old_new_classes.mkdir()
+        run("patched-old-client-source", [stock_javac, *CLIENT_FLAGS, "--patch-module", "java.base=" + str(stock_classes),
+                                           "-d", old_new_classes, old_source], quiet_success=True)
+        if class_tree(old_new_classes) != frozen_classes:
+            raise ValueError("finite old client produces different bytes with added API")
+        negative = args.output / "negative-source/ProgressJobRunnableConflict.java"
+        copy(args.candidate / PREFIX / "src/test/resources/ProgressJobRunnableConflict.java.txt", negative)
+        negative_classes = args.output / "negative-classes"
+        negative_classes.mkdir()
+        stdout, stderr = run("new-runnable-subclass-conflict", [stock_javac, *CLIENT_FLAGS, "-XDrawDiagnostics",
+                                "--patch-module", "java.base=" + str(stock_classes), "-d", negative_classes, negative],
+                               expected_success=False)

+        if not keys or not any(key in ("compiler.err.override.incompatible.ret", "compiler.err.override.weaker.access") for key in keys):

+        if "PASS old Callable" not in stdout:

+            runtime = [java, "-Xmx256m", "-ea", "-Xcheck:jni", "--patch-module", "java.base=" + str(patch)]
+            stdout, _ = run(label + "-old-binary", [*runtime, "-classpath", old_classes, "OldCallableClient"])
+            if "PASS old Callable" not in stdout:

+            match = re.search(r"PASS ProgressJob checks=(\d+)", stdout)
+            if match is None:
+                raise ValueError("core witness did not execute")
+            core_count = int(match.group(1))

+            match = re.search(r"PASS real Eclipse IStatus/Status/MultiStatus checks=(\d+)", stdout)
+            if match is None:

+            counts[label] = {"core_checks": core_count, "real_eclipse_checks": int(match.group(1))}
+        if counts["stock-patched"] != counts["m3-image-patched"]:
+            raise ValueError("runtime witness counts differ")

+        receipt["new_client_classes"] = class_tree(clients)
+        receipt["checks"] = counts
+        receipt["synexia_result_runtime"] = "NOT_RUN: exact IJobResult/AbstractJob/IAdaptable source review only; no stubbed substitute or whole context closure claim"
+        receipt["result"] = "PASS"

+        receipt["failure"] = str(error)

+        raise

+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
